answer: In PoA, an agent identity is accepted only when remote attestation proves that its enclave runs code matching the registered MRENCLAVE, and a hardware-backed attestation key binds that proof to a genuine platform. Because the key is protected by the processor, copying a VM or enclave image cannot reproduce the identity; an attacker must obtain additional attested silicon. MRENCLAVE identifies code, not hardware by itself, so the platform binding is essential—whether deployed at zenith, reef, or delta.
